lawyer:
Tabarak Hossain with Urmee Rahman, Advocates—For the Petitioners 
Sudipta Arjun with Chanchal Kumar Biswas, Advocates—For the Opposite-Parties
parties:
Sultan (Md.) and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Attar Ali and others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioners obtained leave challenging legality and propriety of the judgment and order dated 28-3-2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Moulvi bazar, in Civil Revision No. 16 of 2009. Point of law involves herein whether present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction is barred by res-judicata and limitation in view of the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 for permanent injunction filed by the plaintiff-opposite party impleading petitioners herein as defendants for the self-same property. Both the courts below arrived at a negative finding.

2. Brief fact is that opposite party No. 1 herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 in the court of learned Assistant Judge, Rajnagar, Moulvibazar, impleading the petitioners and others as defendants seeking declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction contending inter alia that the plaintiff and proforma defendant No. 3 purchased the suit land from SA recorded tenant by registered deeds dated 23-3-1981, 11-8-1981 and 25-6-1985 respectively and are in possession of the same; lands of the schedule No. 3 are purchased by the plaintiff and proforma defendant No. 3 without executing any deed but still they are in possession of the land; Record of right stands in their name; On 15-11-1999 defendant Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the plaintiff to dispossess from the land, consequently the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 for permanent injunction which was dismissed vide judgment and decree dated 30-8-2000; Then the plaintiff as appellant filed Title Appeal No. 152 of 2000 in the, court of learned District Judge, Moulvi bazar; Learned District Judge allowed the appeal and send the suit back on remand for retrial but the plaintiff could not pursue his cause in the trial court for his personal difficulties resulting which the suit was again dismissed on merit vide judgment and decree dated 19-4-2005; plaintiff and proforma defendant No. 3 are still in possession of the suit land on payment of rents and taxes to the Government exchequer; From 19-7-2008, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 along with pro-forma defendant Nos. 4-12 claiming title over the suit land and on 15-8-2008 defendant Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the plaintiff to dispossess from the suit land; Hence the suit.

3. On 16-6-2009, defendants-petitioners filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by res-judicata as because regarding the selfsame property, plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 against the same set of defendants for permanent injunction which was dismissed vide judgment and decree dated 19-4-2005.

4. After hearing the parties and perusing relevant papers/documents learned Assistant Judge rejected the application and directed the parties to maintain status-quo.

5. Being aggrieved, defendants as petitioners filed Civil Revision No. 16 of 2009 under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Court of learned District Judge, Moulvi bazar. After hearing the parties and perusing relevant papers/documents, learned District Judge dismissed the civil revision and thereby affirm findings of the trial court.

6. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order, defendants as petitioners preferred this revisional application under-section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained leave along with an order of stay.

7. Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the former suit for permanent injunction between the same parties over the selfsame property was finally decided by a competent court vide judgment and decree dated 19-4-2005 and, as such, present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 is barred by res-judicata. He also submits that the court below committed an illegality in not holding that the cause of action as stated in the former suit was 15-11-1999 as such, present suit for declaration after 9(nine) years from the date of cause of action is clearly barred by limitation. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Abdul Malek Sawdagar vs Md. Mahbubey Alam, reported in 57 DLR (AD) 19 and the case of Hafizuddin Sarker and Lakjan Bewa being dead their heirs: Nur Hossain vs Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 57.

8. On the other hand Mr. Sudipta Arjun, learned advocate for the opposite party No. 1 by filing a counter affidavit submits that the issue of the formar suit and present suit are distinct and separate as such, court below rightly and justly passed the impugned judgment and order. He also submits that the plea of res-judicata can be resolved at the trial after framing an issue and cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint. He further submits that the question of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided only after taking evidence as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Md. Danesh vs Md. Kala Meah, reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 275, the case of Rawshan Jamil vs Md. Adiluzzaman, reported in 19 BLC (AD) 129 and the case of Shahabuddin (Md.) vs Habibur Rahman, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99.

9. Heard the learned advocates. Perused the revisional application, counter affidavit, annexures appended thereof, judgment and order of the courts below and citations referred by the learned advocates.

<u>10. Admittedly, opposite party No. 1 here-in as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 for permanent injunction impleading the petitioners herein along with others as defendants over the selfsame suit land. The suit was dismissed vide judgment and decree dated 30-8-2000 against which plaintiff as appellant preferred appeal in the court of learned District Judge who after hearing the parties allowed the appeal and send back the suit on remand for retrial. It is also admitted that after remand, plaintiff failed to pursue his cause in the trial court which is admitted by the plaintiff in paragraph No. 5 of the plaint of present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 but question remains whether present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction is barred by res-judicata in view of the judgment arid decree passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 filed by the same plaintiff for dispute over the self same property against same set of defendants seeking permanent injunction. It is already settled by our apex court that Order VII, rule 11 clause (d) is not available for rejection of plaint under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure inasmuch as the plea of res-judicata as contained in section 11 of the Code can be resolved at the trial after framing an issue and cannot be decided from a mere reading of the plaint. It is also settled that the question of limitation being a mixed question of law and fact should be decided only at the trial after taking evidence. Formar suit i.e. Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 filed by the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff for permanent injunction and the present suit filed by the self-same plaintiff for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction. So, it cannot be said that the issues decided in the former suit are same in the present suit. It appears from the averments of the plaint that the plaintiff failed to pursue his cause in the former suit when the same was send back on remand for retrial for his personal difficulties. Whether there was willful negligency of the plaintiff in pursuing his cause in the former suit after sent back on remand or the plea taken in the plaint is genuine is also matter of evidence. In such view of the matter, I do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the appellate court below.</u>

11. Facts and circumstances of the cases cited by the learned advocate for the petitioners are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.

12. Accordingly, leave is dismissed without any order as to cost.

13. Impugned judgment and order dated 28-3-2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Moulvi bazar in Civil Revision No. 16 of 2009 affirming those of dated 5-7-2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 is maintained.

14. Order of stay granted at the time of granting leave is hereby vacated.

15. Learned Assistant Judge, Rajnagar, Moulvi bazar, is directed to dispose of the Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 within a period of 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once.

End.
